newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil civil service reform clears committee.
newsitem.headline: Brazil civil service reform clears committee.

text.p: Brazil's civil service reform bill cleared its lower house committee on Wednesday when deputies rejected seven proposed alterations to its text, an official said.
The bill is now due to be sent to the floor of the Chamber of Deputies where it requires two three-fifths majorities before advancing to the Senate.

The official, who asked not to be identified, said the first vote on the chamber floor would only take place after a second round of voting in Brazil's municipal elections which takes place November 15.
Many deputies are expected to remain away from Brasilia over the next three weeks to take part in electoral campaigning.

The reform would allow states and municipalities spending more than 60 percent of receipts on pay to dimiss currently unfireable employees. It would also limit public sector pay packets to a maximum of 10,800 reais a month.
